subject: Materials Science
title: Anti-Reflective Nanostructures
description: A quick win: understand Anti-Reflective Nanostructures.

hook.text: Moth eyes don't reflect light — nanopillar arrays on their surface cancel reflections. Solar cells now copy this trick.

buildup.text: Nanopillars gradually shift refractive index from air to material — eliminating the sharp reflection-causing interface.

discovery.text: Moth-eye nanostructures cut reflection below 1% across all visible wavelengths — better than any thin film coating.

twist.text: These structures help moths hide from predators — they evolved to be invisible, not to improve optics.

climax.text: Anti-reflective nano-textures now improve solar panels, camera lenses, and display screens — bio-inspired photonics.

punchline.text: Moths evolved the perfect anti-glare screen — eons before we needed one.

quiz.question: How do moth-eye nanostructures reduce reflection?
options: Gradually changing refractive index eliminates the sharp interface causing reflection
They scatter light in random directions
